text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - apigw.eu-west-1 returning 502/504s since 14:03 UTC, >20% error rate. Paging @maria (sre-oncall) :rotating_light:

maria: saw it on dashboards, spike started ~14:02 UTC. Latency also climbed on edge. I'm grabbing logs + routing map.

devon: I'm on standby, can take traffic routing if needed. Which customers affected?

priya-cs: CS reports multiple customers with failed requests, top impacted: AcmeCorp, NovaPay — their requests hit 502s. Customers started reporting ~14:05 UTC.

maria: quick facts: 502s concentrated on ingress nodes behind apigw-eu-azb. Backend health looks green for most services. suspect upstream proxy or edge mux.

james: pulling a sample:
```
[14:06:12] apigw-eu-azb proxy: upstream reset while reading response header (errno=104)
[14:06:13] apigw-eu-azb conn: TLS handshake timeout to backend 10.2.34.56:443
```

maria: OK — TLS handshakes + connection resets, could be a cert rotation or a kernel limit on connections. Checking node kernel logs and SNI metrics.

ops-bot: runbook suggestion: set circuit-breaker to 70% and divert 40% traffic to apigw-eu-azc as temporary fallback. Command: `infra router set-weight apigw-eu-azb=60 apigw-eu-azc=40`

maria: doing weighted shift now, will monitor. Also enabling extra proxy worker threads on azb nodes: `ssh proxy@azb-1 sudo systemctl restart proxy --now` (rolling).

devon: I'll pre-warm a secondary pool and spin up 4 more proxy containers in eu-west. K8s command: `kubectl -n apigw scale deploy proxy-eu --replicas=28`

priya-cs: customers asking for ETA, any idea how long to stabilize?

maria: initial mitigation in progress — if weighted routing + scale works we should see drop within 2-5m. If not, fallback to legacy edge (manual route) and open a mitigation ticket to onboard traffic to us-west for worst-case.

incident-bot: telemetry: error rate dropped to 12% after initial shift (14:09 UTC). Latency still elevated for some percentiles.

james: logs show some short-lived cert verify failures to a specific upstream pool (upstream-id: pool-17). Looking into pool health: `upstreamctl status pool-17` shows intermittent connect failures.

maria: temporarily circuit-break pool-17 at LB layer to reduce retries: `upstreamctl set-down pool-17` — will coordinate with teams owning that pool.

devon: scaled proxies are up, new containers showing successful handshakes to backends. Traffic at azc increased as expected. Monitoring for regressions.

priya-cs: I'm telling affected customers we've deployed mitigations and are monitoring; will follow up with timeline after stabilization.

maria: handing off to @devon for next 30m for live mitigation and RCA collection. I'll update incident channel and create an incident ticket. Can whoever touched pool-17 (backup team) please standby for a follow-up?

devon: taking over. Next actions: keep weighted routing at 60/40 for 10m, keep pool-17 down, gather full tcpdump + proxy stacktrace if we see any reflare. tagging @tanvi for kernel/socket limits on azb nodes.

tanvi: on it — checking ulimit and ephemeral port exhaustion. Will post findings.

incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty incident ACK by devon at 14:12 UTC.

maria: brief summary for postmortem: root cause candidate: transient upstream TLS/connect errors concentrated on pool-17 causing apigw retries and proxy resource exhaustion -> 502/504 surge. Mitigations: weighted routing, scale proxies, circuit-break pool-17, restart proxy workers. Actions logged in incident ticket INF-2026-112.

devon: confirmed stable for now, error rate down to 3% at 14:19 UTC. I'll keep monitoring and start gathering traces + request IDs to hand to pool owners.

priya-cs: I'll prepare a customer-facing note; will wait for final RCA before sending.

maria: thanks team. If anything flares I'll rejoin. Otherwise devon will lead the follow-up. :white_check_mark:
